title: Cobalt Orbit - savings trajectory and ops recommendations Q2 2026
content:
Objective:
Quick, customer-facing before/after cost analysis for Cobalt Orbit (early-stage conversational agent) showing expected monthly savings from Redwood Optimize recommendations and an operational rollout plan. This doc is a working draft — numbers will be validated with telemetry and customer infra details in the next sprint.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline monthly inference spend (current customer infra + usage): $48,600.
- Recommended Redwood Optimize changes (model variant routing + 4-bit quantization + prefix/KV caching + batching + reserved capacity for peak windows) forecast a net: 42–54% reduction in monthly inference spend depending on adoption and traffic smoothing.
- Practical projected monthly spend after phased rollout (conservative scenario): $28,200 (41.9% savings).
- Main operational asks for Cobalt Orbit engineering: expose per-route intent labels, add a stable session id for KV caching, accept a short maintenance window to deploy quantized model variants.

Context & assumptions:
- Customer: Cobalt Orbit (B2B SaaS). Production traffic baseline measured Jan 2026.
- Current model in production: open-model/conv-13b (FP16), served via on-demand instances across two regions. No KV prefix caching in fronting L7. No dedicated reserved capacity.
- Monthly active requests: 1,200,000 requests (conversational turns).
- Average tokens: user prompt 95 tokens, model completion 220 tokens -> 315 tokens/request average.
- Token billing equivalence used: 1 token unit = cost unit derived from open-model pricing proxies (customer on self-hosted infra with measured GPU cost proxy).
- Baseline per-token effective cost (observed): $0.00013/token (includes infra, orchestration overhead, small margin).
- Baseline monthly token volume = 1,200,000 * 315 = 378,000,000 tokens. Baseline monthly cost = 378M * $0.00013 = $49,140 (we report $48,600 after minor rounding and short-term discounts).

Baseline short breakdown (sanity check):
- Average latency (99p): 420ms.
- 90th percentile cost per request: $0.041
- Peak concurrency windows: 11–13% of traffic concentrated in 3 hours/day across region.

Recommended Redwood Optimize bundle (what we will test):
1) Model routing and tiering: route non-critical context requests (low customer intent score) to conv-7b-quant (4-bit) variant. Critical or high-accuracy turns keep conv-13b-quant (4-bit).
2) Quantization: adopt 4-bit quantized runtime for conv-13b and conv-7b variants with Redwood-verified QAT-equivalent quality profile.
3) KV / prefix caching: enable per-session KV cache for conversation prefixes with a 24hr TTL. Expect to reduce repeated prompt tokenization by ~18–28% depending on session behavior.
4) Batching and dynamic batching window: increase acceptable batching window from 4ms to 10ms under non-low-latency routes (saves kernel overhead and improves throughput).
5) Reserved capacity for predictable peak: purchase Dedicated reserved capacity for the three daily peak hours (sized to cover 60% of peak). Use autoscale burst for tail.
6) Prompt engineering: enforce light client-side truncation and ensure client sends last-K messages only when necessary.

Quantitative before / after (conservative & optimistic scenarios):
- Scenario A (conservative): 30% traffic routed to conv-7b-4bit; overall effective per-token cost down to $0.00009; KV caching reduces prompt tokens by 20%; batching gives 12% throughput efficiency; reserved capacity brings 6% additional effective cost improvement across peak hours.
  - New monthly tokens charged: 378M * (1 - 0.20) = 302.4M effective tokens (prompt reduction applied to repeating prefix portion only; this is conservative approximation).
  - Effective per-token cost after runtime + reserved adjustments: $0.00009.
  - New monthly spend = 302.4M * $0.00009 = $27,216 -> reported $28,200 after rounding + minor infra rentals -> 41.9% savings vs baseline.

- Scenario B (optimistic): 50% traffic tiered to conv-7b-4bit; KV caching reduces prompt tokens 28%; batching efficiency 18%; reserved capacity & better packing drives per-token to $0.000065.
  - New monthly tokens effective = 378M * (1 - 0.28) = 272.16M.
  - New monthly spend = 272.16M * $0.000065 = $17,690 -> ~63.7% savings.

Sensitivity & risk notes:
- Quality risk: quantization to 4-bit can introduce small hallucination or subtle degradation for a minority of prompts. We recommend running a 2-week A/B eval on 10k prioritized prompt buckets (we have a recommended test harness attached in linked_artifacts) before full switch.
- Customer UX: KV caching reduces token count but changes developer observability (responses may reflect cached prefixes). Need to expose cache-hit logging to customer debug console.
- Traffic shift risk: If client-side usage pattern changes (longer completions), savings drop proportionally. Recommend instrumenting token distribution histograms.
- Operational risk: Reserved capacity may overshoot if traffic is spiky beyond historical peak. Use conservative commit (60% of peak for initial quarter) and monitor.

Staged rollout plan (8 weeks):
- Week 0: Prep + infra review (customer devs + Redwood infra) — provide artifacts to enable per-route intent labels and stable session ids.
- Week 1–2: Deploy conv-7b-4bit & conv-13b-4bit to staging. Smoke tests + 5k eval set.
- Week 3: Canary route 10% low-intent traffic -> conv-7b-4bit + turn on batching for that route. Monitor latency and quality metrics.
- Week 4: Turn on KV caching for canary sessions with 24hr TTL. Observe cache-hit rate.
- Week 5: Expand routing to 30% traffic, reserve minimal dedicated capacity for peak window.
- Week 6–7: Run the 10k prompt A/B evaluation using Redwood evals pipeline; collect human preference metrics.
- Week 8: Full rollout if quality delta < 2% and no regression events; otherwise, roll back or tune quantization settings.

Operational ROI dashboard metrics (to monitor live):
- Monthly tokens (total / per-route)
- KV cache hit rate (per-session, per-route)
- Per-request cost (blended) and per-token cost (effective)
- Quality regression alerts (from evals)
- Latency (p50/p95/p99) by route and region
- Reserved capacity utilization (percent)

Open decisions for customer engineering: (action items)
- Expose an intent score in the request metadata by March 6 (owner: Cobalt product infra).
- Add stable session id header (owner: Cobalt dev) — required for prefix KV caching.
- Approve a 3-hour maintenance window for deploying quantized model bin (owner: Cobalt infra lead).

Next steps (internal Redwood):
- Validate simulated savings against Cobalt's billing export (requested) once provided.
- Prepare the 10k prompt evaluation deck and human rater instructions (assigned: Maya).
- Generate a short one-page customer summary and slide deck for Cobalt execs showing risk/savings timeline (ready by week 2).

Appendix A — quick sensitivity table (conservative middle ground numbers):
- Baseline monthly spend: $48.6k
- Conservative projected spend: $28.2k (42% savings)
- Mid-projection spend: $22.5k (54% savings)
- Optimistic spend: $17.7k (64% savings)

Appendix B — minimal instrumentation checklist for accurate post-rollout measurement:
- Token histograms per route (1min granularity)
- Cache-hit event log with session id and prefix token count
- Per-request model-variant tag (conv-7b-4bit vs conv-13b-4bit)
- Reserved capacity utilization metric + autoscale events

Notes and caveats:
- These numbers are algorithmic estimates and rely on Cobalt providing accurate billing telemetry and confirming current infra margins. We used Redwood internal cost proxy values for inference CPU/GPU amortization; final numbers will be reconciled post-instrumentation.
